title: Six Supply-Chain Translation Prompts
primary_reader: An early- or mid-career supply-chain practitioner who wants to become more cross-functional but does not know which adjacent working language to learn next.

reader_contract.reader_moment: You hear 'get cross-functional exposure' but cannot connect that advice to the decision your own work hands to someone else.
reader_contract.reader_payoff: A practical way to choose one adjacent supply-chain language to learn next.
reader_contract.decision_question: Which adjacent decision should I understand better to make my current work more useful?
reader_contract.glance_3s: Do not learn all of supply chain. Learn the next decision your work affects.
reader_contract.scan_10s: Six functions connect through the decisions they hand onward.
reader_contract.use_30s: Locate your current function, follow one directional transfer, and ask which decision your work makes harder for the next owner.

scope.in_scope: A bounded career-development and collaboration framework for selecting one adjacent function to understand better.
scope.not_for: It is not a universal career ladder, competency benchmark, organisational design, or guarantee that every role should follow the same handoff.
scope.assumptions: The reader adapts the language to their own company structure, role scope, and current decision rights.

truth_contract.basis: An editorial synthesis of six common supply-chain functions and the next decision each role often needs to understand.
truth_contract.scope: The map is a conversation and learning aid, not an empirical model of career progression or functional ownership.
truth_contract.not_claiming: It does not prove that one sequence is optimal, that every company uses these functions, or that cross-functional literacy causes a career outcome.

visual_argument.spatial_claim: Each function has an adjacent decision language that can make its next cross-functional conversation more useful.
visual_argument.why_shape_truthful: An asymmetric atlas lets a reader start at one function and trace one useful hop to a decision language, without pretending that the six links are verified receiver ownership or a universal operating sequence.
visual_argument.anti_misread: Do not show this as a ladder, wheel, fixed network of functional ownership, or prescribed career rotation sequence.

modules.title: Procurement → demand signal
modules.reader_action: Ask how the demand signal changes the supplier conversation before treating price or lead time as the only input.

modules.title: Planning → capacity constraint
modules.reader_action: Translate a plan into the capacity question that manufacturing or a supplier must resolve.

modules.title: Manufacturing → delivery promise
modules.reader_action: Connect the production constraint to the commitment that logistics or the customer-facing team must manage.

modules.title: Logistics → customer commitment
modules.reader_action: Frame movement and freight choices through the commitment they protect or put at risk.

modules.title: Analytics → operator decision
modules.reader_action: Ask which operator decision should become easier before building another report or model.

modules.title: Strategy → frontline workflow
modules.reader_action: Test whether the strategic idea can be explained as a changed frontline decision or handoff.

claims.text: Procurement can use the demand signal as an adjacent language for a better supplier conversation.

evidence.rationale: A bounded editorial framework, not a documented performance outcome.

claims.text: Planning can use the capacity constraint as an adjacent language for a more workable plan.

evidence.rationale: A bounded editorial framework, not a documented performance outcome.

claims.text: Manufacturing can use the delivery promise as an adjacent language for clearer handoffs.

evidence.rationale: A bounded editorial framework, not a documented performance outcome.

claims.text: Logistics can use the customer commitment as an adjacent language for prioritising movement choices.

evidence.rationale: A bounded editorial framework, not a documented performance outcome.

claims.text: Analytics can use the operator decision as an adjacent language for making analysis more usable.

evidence.rationale: A bounded editorial framework, not a documented performance outcome.

claims.text: Strategy can use the frontline workflow as an adjacent language for testing implementation reality.

evidence.rationale: A bounded editorial framework, not a documented performance outcome.

boundary_or_exception.statement: Do not treat a map of adjacent languages as a reason to become shallow across everything. Some decisions require deep specialist ownership; this guide only helps choose the next useful conversation.
boundary_or_exception.reader_response: Choose one adjacent handoff, then ask the relevant specialist which real decision, project, or meeting would teach it safely.

next_action: Before your next meeting, ask: "What decision does my work make harder for the next owner?" Then ask that owner what they need from your work.

motion.reason: The map needs stable reading time and a reader should be able to return to any handoff without waiting through an animation.
